nodes.name: HIGHLIGHT_SCALE
nodes.summary: How much a search-focused node is enlarged, so it stands out from its neighbours without a shader change.

nodes.name: DIM_FACTOR
nodes.summary: How far the rest of the graph fades when a node is selected — its RGB is multiplied by this, so a low value pushes unselected nodes toward black while the selection and its edge-connected neighbours stay at full 1.0.

nodes.name: FOCUS_STANDOFF
nodes.summary: Distance the camera sits from a node it focuses on — the default framing.

nodes.name: PICK_MIN_RADIUS
nodes.summary: Smallest clickable node radius in pixels — a distant node's sprite can shrink below the cursor's precision, so picking is forgiving.

nodes.name: PICK_EDGE_THRESHOLD
nodes.summary: How close, in pixels, the cursor must fall to an edge line to select it.

nodes.name: MAX_LABELS
nodes.summary: Cap on how many node labels are drawn per frame when labels are on, so a large repository stays interactive; nearer/earlier nodes win.

nodes.name: LABEL_OFFSET
nodes.summary: Points a label sits above its node's projected centre.

nodes.name: project_labels
nodes.signature: fn project_labels( camera: &Camera, graph: &GraphData, visible: &KindVisibility, selected: Option<usize>, selection_depth: u32, width: f32, height: f32, pixels_per_point: f32, ) -> Vec<(egui::Pos2, String)>
nodes.summary: Projects each node's name to a screen position for the label overlay. A free function taking the pieces it needs (rather than `&self`) so it can run while `self.active` is mutably borrowed for the egui pass. Nodes behind the camera or outside the view frustum are skipped; positions are returned in egui points (physical pixels divided by `pixels_per_point`).

nodes.name: report_throughput
nodes.summary: Logs frames per second every [`REPORT_INTERVAL`]. The GUI already shows this, but a window is not always something you can read a number off — under a benchmark, over a remote session, or while the frame rate is low enough that the panel itself is hard to catch. Averaged over the interval rather than taken from the last frame, which on a loaded device is noisy.

nodes.name: sync_from_gpu
nodes.summary: Brings host node state back up to date after a GPU layout has been running. A GPU step leaves the authoritative positions in the node buffer and never touches `self.graph`. Without this, switching to a CPU layout would resume from wherever the last CPU step left off and discard everything the GPU did. It stalls the pipeline, so it happens only on a layout change, never on the frame path.

nodes.name: dim_mask
nodes.summary: Builds the per-node dim mask for a selection of `idx`: `1.0` for the selected node and every node sharing an edge with it, `DIM_FACTOR` for the rest.

nodes.name: clear_dim
nodes.summary: Restores full brightness to every node and edge.

nodes.name: apply_visibility
nodes.summary: Uploads the per-node visibility mask from the current kind filters, so the shader hides the unchecked kinds' nodes and their edges. A no-op without a sidecar (no kinds to filter) or a window.

nodes.name: reconcile_labels_and_update
nodes.summary: Keeps the Labels and Update toggles consistent, run once after the GUI. Labels are hidden while the layout runs (they would lag the live GPU positions), so switching Labels on while Update is running stops the layout; and any transition to stopped schedules a one-off position sync so the labels reappear exactly on the settled nodes.

Placing `target` at `(0, 0, -standoff)` — the same framing the default camera gives the origin — means `position = (0,0,-standoff) - targ…

nodes.summary: Builds a searchable graph from the text of `rkg export`'s `repo.edges` and `nodes.tsv` files. Shared by the native file loader and browser viewer so the two surfaces accept precisely the same artifact format.

nodes.name: parse_sidecar
nodes.summary: Parses a `nodes.tsv` sidecar (`index<TAB>id<TAB>name<TAB>kind<TAB>path`) into a dense `Vec<NodeMeta>` ordered by the `index` column. `#` comment lines skipped.

nodes.name: parse_span
nodes.summary: Parses a `start-end` span cell into a line range, or `None` if empty/malformed.

nodes.name: parse_indexed_edges
nodes.summary: Parses an edge list of integer index pairs (as [`load_with_sidecar`] expects), validating that every index is within `node_count`.

nodes.name: label_order_is_lexicographic
nodes.summary: Labels sort lexicographically, not numerically — "10" precedes "9". That is the original's behaviour and callers depend on it only for determinism, not for ordering, so it is pinned here rather than fixed.

nodes.name: Node
nodes.summary: One graph node, 48 bytes, 16-byte aligned. Field order and padding mirror the original `VertexData`/`GraphicData`: `vec4 position; vec4 color; float size; float dx, dy, dz;`

nodes.name: Edge
nodes.summary: A directed edge over dense node indices.

nodes.name: Csr
nodes.summary: Undirected adjacency in compressed sparse row form. The attractive-force pass gathers per node rather than scattering per edge — that is what removes the read-modify-write race the original's `fruchtermanreingold_attractive.comp` had — and a gather needs each node's neighbour list contiguously. Both arrays upload to the GPU as-is.

nodes.name: build
nodes.signature: pub fn build(node_count: usize, edges: &[Edge]) -> Self
nodes.summary: Builds the adjacency for `node_count` nodes from a directed edge list, treating every edge as undirected.

nodes.name: neighbors_of
nodes.summary: Neighbours of `node`.

nodes.name: NodeCategory
nodes.summary: What a node represents, when loaded from a knowledge-graph sidecar. Mirrors `rkg_core::NodeKind` but is duplicated here to keep `gv-graph` a leaf crate the knowledge-graph crates depend on, not the other way around.

nodes.name: from_tag
nodes.summary: Parses the lowercase tag written in `nodes.tsv`.

nodes.name: tag_short
nodes.summary: Short lowercase label for display in the search list.

nodes.name: color
nodes.summary: A fixed, legible RGBA colour per category, used when the loaded graph carries kinds instead of anonymous ids.

nodes.name: NodeMeta
nodes.summary: Per-node metadata from a knowledge-graph sidecar (`nodes.tsv`). Empty on a plain edge-list load; populated by [`loader::load_with_sidecar`], which is what the searchable browser reads.

nodes.name: GraphData
nodes.summary: A loaded graph: node state, edges, adjacency, and the original string ids.

nodes.name: from_edges
nodes.signature: pub fn from_edges(node_count: usize, edges: Vec<Edge>, rng_seed: u64) -> GraphData
nodes.summary: Builds a graph from an edge list over `node_count` nodes, scattered with [`seed::SeedOptions::default`] at the given seed.

nodes.name: dumbbell
nodes.summary: Two nodes joined by one edge — the smallest graph with a force balance, which settles at a separation near `k`.

nodes.name: triangle
nodes.summary: A triangle: every pair joined, so the layout should tend to equilateral.

nodes.name: dust
nodes.summary: `node_count` nodes and no edges — repulsion only, so it should expand without bound until gravity balances it.

nodes.name: distance
nodes.signature: pub fn distance(graph: &GraphData, a: usize, b: usize) -> f32
nodes.summary: Euclidean distance between two nodes, ignoring the padding lane.

nodes.name: all_finite
nodes.summary: True if every node position is finite — the cheapest guard against a layout that has diverged or divided by zero.

nodes.name: scatter
nodes.signature: pub fn scatter(graph: &mut GraphData, options: SeedOptions)
nodes.summary: Places, colours and sizes every node in `graph`.

nodes.name: colorize_by_kind
nodes.summary: Overrides node colours from their knowledge-graph kind, when the graph was loaded with a sidecar (`GraphData::meta`). Call after [`scatter`] to keep the random positions/sizes but replace the random colours with legible per-kind ones. A no-op when `meta` is empty (a plain edge-list load).

nodes.name: KindVisibility
nodes.summary: Which node kinds are drawn in the scene. Unchecking one hides its nodes, their edges, and their labels. All visible by default.

nodes.name: allows
nodes.signature: pub fn allows(&self, kind: NodeCategory) -> bool
nodes.summary: Whether nodes of `kind` are currently drawn. Unknown kinds always show.

nodes.name: SearchState
nodes.summary: Persistent state for the node search panel, owned by the app across frames.

nodes.name: MAX_RESULTS
nodes.summary: How many matches the panel lists before it stops, to keep the frame cheap on a large repository.

nodes.name: FILTER_KINDS
nodes.summary: The kinds offered in the search filter, with their labels.

nodes.name: LayoutChoice
nodes.summary: Which algorithm the picker currently has selected. The original keyed this on a bare `int` (0, 1, 2, 3) shared between the radio buttons and a `switch` with no default case, so an unexpected value returned an uninitialised pointer.

nodes.name: ALL
nodes.signature: pub const ALL: [Self; 5] = [ Self::FrGpu, Self::FrGpuBarnesHut, Self::FrCpu, Self::FrBarnesHut, Self::Random, ];

nodes.name: is_gpu
nodes.summary: True if this layout runs as compute passes rather than on the host.

nodes.name: is_approximate
nodes.summary: True if this layout approximates repulsion with a tree rather than summing every pair.

nodes.name: is_implemented
nodes.summary: Whether this layout actually runs what its label says. The picker offers every variant so the set is visible and the CLI is stable, but two are not written yet and quietly run something else. Keeping that on the type — rather than only in a `log::warn!` nobody reads — is what stops the picker from claiming to do something it does not. Delete an arm as its implementation lands.

nodes.name: falls_back_to
nodes.summary: What actually runs when [`Self::is_implemented`] is false.

nodes.name: slug
nodes.summary: Short name accepted on the command line.

nodes.name: GuiState
nodes.summary: Everything the panels read or write, in one borrow.

nodes.name: GuiActions
nodes.summary: Set when a panel asks the app to do something it cannot do itself.

nodes.name: SPEED_RANGE
nodes.summary: Bounds the original clamped `speed` into inside its `InputFloat` handler.

nodes.name: MIN_AREA
nodes.summary: `area` must stay positive: `k` is proportional to it, and a negative `k` inverts every force. The original clamped this too.

nodes.name: MIN_MOVE_SPEED
nodes.summary: Bounds for the camera move-speed setting (world units per frame).

nodes.name: MIN_WHEEL_ZOOM
nodes.summary: Bounds for the mouse-wheel zoom multiplier.

nodes.name: MAX_SELECTION_DEPTH
nodes.summary: Keep selection traversal bounded on large repository graphs.

nodes.name: PANEL_WIDTH
nodes.summary: Width of each edge-anchored panel window.

nodes.name: PANEL_MARGIN
nodes.summary: Inset of each panel from the window edge it anchors to.

nodes.name: SECTION_GAP
nodes.summary: Vertical padding placed around each section so they read as evenly spaced.

nodes.name: section
nodes.signature: fn section(ui: &mut egui::Ui, title: &str, add: impl FnOnce(&mut egui::Ui))
nodes.summary: A titled block inside a panel, with even padding above and below and a divider, so stacked sections space consistently.

nodes.name: draw
nodes.signature: pub fn draw(ctx: &egui::Context, state: GuiState<'_>) -> GuiActions
nodes.summary: Draws every panel and reports what the user asked for. The GUI is sorted into two edge-anchored windows — configuration pinned to the right edge, browsing to the left — leaving the centre clear for the graph. Each stacks titled sections with uniform spacing.

nodes.name: draw_search
nodes.signature: fn draw_search( ui: &mut egui::Ui, search: &mut SearchState, nodes_meta: &[NodeMeta], actions: &mut GuiActions, )
nodes.summary: Draws the node search controls: a query box, a kind filter, per-kind scene visibility, and a scrollable list of matches that focus the camera when clicked. Rendered inside the left panel's "Search" section.

nodes.name: draw_inspector
nodes.signature: fn draw_inspector(ui: &mut egui::Ui, meta: &NodeMeta, actions: &mut GuiActions)
nodes.summary: Draws the metadata for a clicked node inside the left panel's "Node" section.

nodes.name: search_matches
nodes.signature: fn search_matches( nodes_meta: &[NodeMeta], query: &str, kind_filter: Option<NodeCategory>, ) -> Vec<usize>
nodes.summary: Indices of nodes whose name or path contains `query` (case-insensitive) and match `kind_filter`, ranked with name-prefix hits first. An empty query with no filter returns nothing, so the list starts empty rather than dumping the whole repository.

nodes.name: clamp_params
nodes.summary: Applies the clamps [`draw`] enforces, so they can be checked without a rendering context.

nodes.name: run_draw
nodes.signature: fn run_draw(config: &mut AppConfig, params: &mut LayoutParams, choice: &mut LayoutChoice) -> GuiActions
nodes.summary: Runs the panels headlessly. `egui::Context::run_ui` needs no window, so the real `draw` is exercised — not a stand-in.

nodes.name: meta
nodes.signature: fn meta(name: &str, path: &str, kind: NodeCategory) -> NodeMeta

nodes.name: SPEED_DIVISOR
nodes.summary: Divisor applied to `speed` before it scales a displacement. Named `SPEED_DIVISOR` in the original's GLSL.

nodes.name: AREA_MULTIPLIER
nodes.summary: Multiplier applied to `area` when deriving the ideal edge length `k`. Named `AREA_MULTIPLICATOR` in the original's GLSL.

nodes.name: LayoutParams
nodes.summary: The three knobs the original exposed in its "Graph settings" ImGui panel, plus the 2D/3D switch that lived in the "Algorithms" panel.

nodes.name: k
nodes.signature: pub fn k(&self, node_count: usize) -> f32
nodes.summary: Ideal edge length: `k = (AREA_MULTIPLIER * area) / (1 + n)`.

nodes.name: max_displace
nodes.summary: Per-step displacement ceiling, before the speed scale is applied.

nodes.name: speed_scale
nodes.summary: The factor displacements are scaled by each step.

nodes.name: separation
nodes.signature: pub fn separation(a: &[f32; 4], b: &[f32; 4], three_d: bool) -> ([f32; 3], f32)
nodes.summary: Separation between two nodes: the vector from `a` to `b`, and its length. In 2D the z lane is dropped rather than merely ignored, so a node that still carries a stale z from a 3D run cannot influence the distance.

nodes.name: attraction
nodes.signature: pub fn attraction( index: usize, positions: &[[f32; 4]], adjacency: &gv_graph::Csr, k: f32, three_d: bool, ) -> [f32; 3]
nodes.summary: Attraction on node `i`: `d² / k` toward each of its neighbours. Gathered over the node's CSR row, so this invocation writes only its own displacement — the structure that removes the original's per-edge race.

nodes.name: integrate
nodes.signature: pub fn integrate( graph: &mut GraphData, displacements: Vec<[f32; 3]>, params: &LayoutParams, k: f32, )
nodes.summary: Applies gravity, the speed scale and the displacement ceiling, then writes the new positions. Shared by every CPU layout so they cannot drift in how a step is closed out: only the force accumulation above differs between them, and that is the only thing that should.

nodes.name: CpuLayout
nodes.summary: A layout that advances the node array in host memory.

nodes.name: NONE
nodes.summary: Absent index, for `escape` and `body`.

nodes.name: MAX_DEPTH
nodes.summary: Depth at which subdivision gives up and the cell becomes an aggregate. Coincident bodies never separate no matter how far the tree subdivides, so without a cap the build recurses until it runs out of stack. At this depth a cell spans the root width over 2²⁴, which is far below any distance the force computation can distinguish, so lumping whatever is left changes nothing: bodies that close are at …

nodes.name: Cell
nodes.summary: One cell of the flattened tree: an aggregate body plus where to skip to. 32 bytes, `repr(C)`, and laid out so the WGSL mirror needs no padding games — `center` is three separate lanes followed by `mass`, which packs as two 16-byte chunks with no implicit alignment gaps.

nodes.name: Octree
nodes.summary: The flattened tree.

nodes.name: LEVELS
nodes.summary: Bits of Morton code per axis, and so the number of levels the tree can distinguish. 21 fits three axes in a `u64` and resolves the root cube to one part in two million, far finer than any distance the forces resolve.

nodes.name: spread
nodes.summary: Spreads 21 bits so each occupies every third bit position. The standard Morton dilation: five shift-and-mask rounds, which beats a per-bit loop by roughly an order of magnitude and is what makes computing 100k codes free next to sorting them.

nodes.name: morton
nodes.signature: fn morton(position: [f32; 3], center: [f32; 3], half: f32) -> u64
nodes.summary: Morton (Z-order) code of a position within the root cube. x lands in the low bit of each three-bit group, matching [`octant_of`], so the code's digits *are* the octant path from the root — which is what lets the build read the tree straight off a sorted array.

nodes.name: digit
nodes.signature: fn digit(code: u64, depth: u32) -> usize
nodes.summary: The octant digit of a code at a given depth, root first.

nodes.name: emit
nodes.signature: fn emit( &mut self, lo: usize, hi: usize, depth: u32, center: [f32; 3], half: f32, ) -> ([f64; 3], u32)
nodes.summary: Emits the subtree covering `keys[lo..hi]` in depth-first order and returns its summed positions and body count. Summed in f64: 100k single-precision additions into one accumulator lose enough low bits to move a centre of mass visibly.

nodes.name: build
nodes.summary: Builds the tree over `positions`. In 2D the caller is expected to have already flattened z, so that the tree subdivides in the plane the forces actually act in.

nodes.name: repulsion
nodes.signature: pub fn repulsion(&self, body: u32, position: [f32; 3], k: f32, theta: f32) -> [f32; 3]
nodes.summary: Repulsion on `body` at `position`, as `k² / d` away from every other body, with distant subtrees aggregated. `theta` is the opening angle: a cell is accepted whole when its width over the distance to it falls below `theta`. Zero opens everything and degrades to brute force.

nodes.name: bounding_cube
nodes.summary: Centre and half-width of a cube containing every position.

nodes.name: octant_of
nodes.summary: Which of the eight octants of `center` a position falls in. Only used to pin the Morton bit convention in the tests — the build reads octants out of the code's digits instead.

nodes.name: child_center
nodes.signature: fn child_center(center: [f32; 3], half: f32, octant: usize) -> [f32; 3]
nodes.summary: Centre of the given octant of a parent, where `half` is the *child's* half-width.

nodes.name: brute_force
nodes.signature: fn brute_force(positions: &[[f32; 3]], body: usize, k: f32) -> [f32; 3]

nodes.name: cloud
nodes.summary: Deterministic pseudo-random cloud, so failures reproduce.

nodes.name: step
nodes.signature: fn step(&mut self, graph: &mut GraphData, params: &LayoutParams)

nodes.name: step
nodes.signature: fn step(&mut self, graph: &mut GraphData, params: &LayoutParams)

nodes.name: run
nodes.signature: fn run(graph: &mut GraphData, params: &LayoutParams, steps: usize)
